title.narrative: Assam State Secondary Healthcare Initiative for Service Delivery Transformation (ASSIST) Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Assam State Secondary Healthcare Initiative for Service Delivery Transformation (ASSIST) Project for India is to strengthen management capacity, access to, and quality of the secondary healthcare system in Assam. The project comprises of three components. The first component, strengthened management capacity of health systems at state, district, and facility level consists of following sub-components: (i) internal performance agreements (IPAs) to strengthen management capacity; and (ii) technical support and project operating costs to strengthen management capacity. The second component is improved access to and quality of essential services in existing secondary facilities. The third component, enhanced access to and structural quality of secondary care will invest in: (a) upgrading up to 10 community health center (CHCs) and sub-district hospitals (SDHs) to district hospital (DH) following national guidelines and provision of medical equipment and goods to enhance equitable access to secondary care, and (b) incremental operating costs of these newly upgraded facilities to improve structural quality of secondary care.
To strengthen management capacity, access to, and quality of the secondary healthcare system in Assam.

condition.narrative: The PIE shall ensure that it provides counterpart funding of 20 percent of the estimated Project cost for the implementation ofProject activities and share the corresponding financial information with the Bank at the end of every fiscal year for the Bank'sreview and monitoring of such contribution.
The PIE shall ensure that the audit of the Financial Statements shall be carried out by a firm of Chartered Accountants.

The PIE shall maintain throughout the period of project implementation, AHIDMS, the State Project Management Unit (“SPMU”), headedby a Project Director and comprising of experienced and qualified staff and consultants, in sufficient numbers and under terms ofreference acceptable to the World Bank, which shall be responsible for day-to-day project implementation and monitoring, and shallhave functions and responsibilities acceptable to the World Bank, including, inter alia: (a) preparing Annual Work Plans andBudgets and ensuring all project activities are planned, financed and implemented accordingly; (b) preparing the POM and ensuringproject implementation is in accordance with the POM; (c) ensuring that procurement and financial management activities are carriedout in a timely manner in accordance with the POM; (d) ensuring compliance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan(ESCP); (e) monitoring project activities; and (f) preparing project progress reports and ensuring their timely submission to theWorld Bank.

The PIE shall maintain throughout the period of project implementation, the Project Executive Committee, chaired by the Chairman ofthe executive committee of AHIDMS; which committee shall have composition, functions, and responsibilities acceptable to the WorldBank, including providing regular monitoring and necessary approvals for the day-to-day implementation of the project.

The PIE shall prepare and adopt a manual (“IPA Grants Manual”), in a manner and substance satisfactory to the World Bank, whichshall set forth the implementation arrangements for the IPA Grants, including, inter alia: (i) eligibility criteria ofBeneficiaries; (ii) procedures and requirements to disburse the IPA Grants; (iii) eligible activities to be financed under the IPAGrants; and (iv) templates for the Internal Performance Agreements. The PIE shall ensure that the activities under Component 1A ofthe project are implemented in accordance with the IPA Grants Manual. The PIE shall not amend, suspend, abrogate, repeal, or waiveany provision of the IPA Grants Manual without prior written approval by the World Bank.

The PIE shall, no later than April 30 of each fiscal year during project implementation, prepare and furnish to the World Bank, anannual program of activities proposed for implementation under the project during the following year, together with a proposedbudget for the purpose, except for the annual work plan and budget for the first year which shall be furnished prior to thecommencement of the relevant activities under the project. The PIE shall exchange views with the Bank on each such proposed annualwork plan for the project, and shall thereafter adopt, and carry out such activities for such following fiscal year as shall havebeen agreed with the World Bank, as such plan may be subsequently revised during such following fiscal year with the prior writtenagreement of the World Bank.

The PIE shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, prepare, approve and adopt a POM in a manner and substancesatisfactory to the World Bank, and thereafter carry out the project in accordance with the provisions of the POM, which manualshall include, inter alia: (i) the details of the project activities including results framework and overall budget; (ii) theproject implementation arrangements; (iii) the IPA Grants Manual; (iv) the format of the interim unaudited financial reports to besubmitted under the project; (v) the project's administrative, accounting, auditing, reporting, financial management andprocurement requirements; (vi) the ESCP; and (vii) the project's monitoring and evaluation, and reporting requirements. The PIEshall not amend, suspend, abrogate, repeal, or waive any provision of the POM without prior written approval by the World Bank.

The PIE shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, recruit, and maintain throughout project implementation,an external verification agency, under terms of reference and with qualifications and experience acceptable to the Bank, to verifythe achievement of indicators/results achieved by the Beneficiaries under the Internal Performance Grant.

The PIE shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, recruit, and maintain until the date set forth in the POM,a project management and technical agency, under terms of reference and with qualifications and experience acceptable to the WorldBank, to provide fiduciary and technical support to the SPMU for the implementation of the project.

The PIE shall: (a) ensure that the project's activities involving collection, storage, usage, and/or processing of Personal Dataare carried out with due regard to the Borrower's existing legal framework and appropriate international data protection andprivacystandards and practices and ensure legitimate, appropriate, and proportionate treatment of such data; (b) in the eventthat, during the implementation of the project, the approval of any new legislation regarding Personal Data protection may have animpact on the activities financed by the Project, ensure that a technical analysis of said impact is conducted and that thenecessary recommendations and adjustments are implemented, as appropriate; and(c) except as may otherwise be explicitly requiredor permitted under the project Loan Agreement, or as may be explicitly requested by the World Bank, in sharing any information,report or document related to the activities described in Schedule 1 to the Loan Agreement, ensure that such information, report ordocument does not include Personal Data.

The Project Implementing Entity (PIE) shall maintain throughout the period of project implementation, the Project SteeringCommittee, chaired by the Chairman of the governing body of AHIDMS; which committee shall have composition, functions, andresponsibilities acceptable to the World Bank, including providing oversight on project implementation; approving and monitoringannual work plans and budgets; and approving the Project Operational Manual (POM).

title.narrative: Secondary care HRH management policies and strategies enacted

comment.narrative: Extent to which there is a current, comprehensive, strategic state secondary HRH plan that outlines policies, laws, and regulations for the health workforce in alignment with state needs and state health policy. Policies and strategies include: (i) Secondary Reviw of existing HRH Policies and identifying Key HRH challenges, (ii) State level enumerated data for HRH in a central server/database, (iii) Functional review of the Department of Health including directorates and NHM, (iv) Revised Transfer, Posting, and Deployment strategy for HRH at secondary health care developed and adopted, (v) Creation of Hospital Manager cadre at District Hospitals, and (vi) Developing a state level HRH management and Strategy Framework.

title.narrative: Technical resources developed and actions taken with project support to strengthen nursing

comment.narrative: Technical resources: They are defined broadly as tools, models, methodologies, strategies and Policy notes. They may include but are not limited to assessments, manuscripts, reports, strategic and operational plans, and training courses/modules. These actions and resources include: (i) an Agency for providing technical support in the areas of pre-service education contracted, (ii) State level vision document (a roadmap) for reforming pre-service nursing education developed, (iii) an Operational Strategy for Developing B.S. colleges of Nursing in the state (Public) developed, (iv) Operational strategy for revival of ANM schools in the state (Public) developed, (v) Implementation of Common Entrance Exam (CEE) for GNM, B.SC, and M.Sc (Public & Private), and (vi) Operational Strategy for establishing Center of Excellence (nursing) in the state developed.

title.narrative: Management capacity of state and district IPA units

baseline.value: Will be assessed when project begins

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure percentage point improvement in average performance score of the state and district management IPA units.

title.narrative: Average performance score of district hospitals

comment.narrative: The performance score is based on the IPA score of district hospitals which comprises (i) structural quality, (ii) process quality, (iii) patient experience, (iv) hospital financial efficiency, (v) management capacity, and (vi) communication and community outreac indicators inclusive of NQAS. The weightage given to each domain are (i) 15%, (ii) 25%, (iii) 20%, (iv) 10%, (v) 20%, and (vi) 10%. Numerator: Total score of the DHs in the last six months implementing IPA. Denominator: Total number of DHs at the beginning of the project.
